title: one tied block to multiple Mirror layers
hypothesis: A single shared linear block wrapped by learned per-depth Givens conjugation can recover layer-specific behavior for a coordinate-aligned depth teacher with fewer serialized inference bytes than independent layers, and can outperform byte-near ordinary tying, rank-1 static per-step LoRA, and shared generated-gain controls at equal updates.
physical_object: One 8x8 shared linear block reused at four logical depths
mirror_coordinate: One learned Givens angle for each logical depth, charged in the model payload
logical_multiplicity: Four depth-specific linear maps from one physical block
controls: shared block with learned per-depth diagonal gain

development.selection_metric: four-layer held-out MSE at a fixed 600 Adam updates, learning rate 0.01

success_gate: On the aligned teacher, all three fresh worlds: Mirror test MSE <= 1.10x untied MSE, <= 1.10x the best shared baseline MSE, and Mirror serialized payload <= 0.80x untied bytes. Report independent teacher separately as a boundary; this is a fixed-update mechanism screen, not a capacity claim.
failure_gate: On development, Mirror misses either the 1.10x quality comparison to untied or 0.80x byte ratio in both worlds, or a byte-near simple shared control matches/lowers MSE. Do not open fresh worlds after this gate.
boundaries: Fixed-update learning-efficiency screen, not near-convergence capacity evidence
Mirror addresses use a single Givens plane
Independent teacher tests the need for private depth parameters
